title: Fractional laser with and without exosomes for hair thinning: a split-scalp trial registered at a Taiwan hospital
headline: A 30-person split-scalp study at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital is testing fractional laser alone against fractional laser plus exosomes on each side of the scalp in androgenetic alopecia; recruiting, no results, exosome product not identified.
evidenceTier: Trial registry record (search listing only; full record not opened)
fit: Hair lane (wildcard): Unknown. The exosome product, source and regulatory status are not stated in the listing I saw.
regions: Taiwan (single site); exosome products have unclear approval status in most markets
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Prices not looked up; cannot judge whether price tracks evidence.
summaryPoints: Observation (registry search listing only; full record not opened): recruiting; n=30; start Dec 2025; primary completion Sept 2027; intervention listed as fractional laser.
Inference: split-scalp design controls for person-level differences but not for laser-side bleed or participant awareness.
Limits: I only saw the search listing; product, dose, outcomes and endpoints are not confirmed.
fitLine: A within-person design is a good start; exosome products are poorly standardised and mostly unregulated as injectables or topicals, which matters more than the laser.
